summary: sitecard serve exposes an SSH shell on the host via public tunnels, open by default
details: When the operator runs `sitecard serve`, gateway.py starts an AsyncSSH server rooted at a chosen workspace directory and bridges it to the public internet through user-selectable relays (srv.us, devtunnels.ms, cloudflared, upterm, ws-relay). The CLI defaults to `--public-access`/`--accept`, which configures the SSH server to accept any client that knows the public URL: `TokenSSHServer.begin_auth` returns False and both password and public-key auth are disabled in accept mode, so anyone who learns the tunnel URL obtains an interactive shell/PTY inside the exported workspace. Authenticated modes (authorized_keys, password) exist but are not the default, and the README states that fresh Sitecard sessions allow public access by default. A separate model-relay subcommand (`-m`) proxies Responses API traffic to the hardcoded upstream `https://chatgpt.com:18080/backend-api/codex`, overridable via `--upstream`; this is documented and user-invoked. The remote-shell capability is the advertised product and only starts when the operator runs the `serve` subcommand (not at install or import time), and there is no lifecycle hook, boot persistence, collateral secret harvesting, or outbound exfiltration to an author-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
